Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner · [LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner Exploitation High
Hunts the exact exploitation primitive Microsoft Threat Intelligence described: the Claude Code Action's in-process Read tool, when steered by an injected prompt, opens /proc/self/environ (or /proc/<pid>/environ) to harvest the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and OIDC credentials. Pre-fix (claude-code-action <2.1.128) the Bubblewrap sandbox + CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB does not cover Read, so the node process serving Claude Code opens /proc directly — a path almost nothing legitimate touches on a build runner. Rationale: Article names the exact primitive: 'eventually authorized to access /proc/self/environ, reading the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'. We pin on the Linux file path regex + node as the actor. The Read tool runs in-process inside node (not via Bash), so the file event is the only signal — there is no child process to pivot on. Corroborated by Flatt Security (flatt.tech) and Hacker News reporting which describe the same /proc/self/environ exfil chain. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/claude-code-github-action-flaw-let-one.html • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/

[LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner Exploitation Medium
Even after the /proc fix in claude-code-action 2.1.128, an attacker who controls the prompt can still steer the Read tool to any path the runner can see. This hunts node — running from the Actions work dir — opening the common secret stores a CI job tends to have on disk: ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc (NPM publish token), ~/.docker/config.json (registry token), ~/.kube/config, ~/.netrc, SSH keys, .env files. Microsoft's article explicitly calls out that 'once an attacker can influence the agent, they might be able to steer it toward sensitive files available inside the CI runner environment'. Rationale: Article: 'once an attacker can influence the agent, they might be able to steer it toward sensitive files available inside the CI runner environment.' We restrict to node spawned from `_work/` or the anthropic action checkout dir so legit user shell activity reading `~/.aws/credentials` doesn't fire. Path list is the GitHub Actions secret canon — npm publish tokens, docker registry creds, GitHub CLI tokens, terraform/pypi publishers — all of which routinely live in runner home dirs. Cross-checked: Flatt's writeup confirms ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + GITHUB_TOKEN + OIDC creds are the named targets, the broader hunt covers what would be next. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/

[LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint Command & Control Medium
Closes the loop on the exfiltration step. The Claude Code Action's legitimate outbound destinations are tightly scoped — api.anthropic.com (LLM calls) and the GitHub control plane (api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io, results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com). When the same node process under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action` reaches anything else on a public IP, an attacker is probably steering it to POST the stolen ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OIDC token to their collection endpoint, or to fetch a second-stage payload to plant into a PR (the docs-XSS scenario from Figure 1). Rationale: Article's threat model is clear: 'the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and potentially other credentials available to the runner' get exfiltrated, and the same agent primitive 'create_pull_request_from_changes' lets the attacker reach an external endpoint to receive them or fetch payloads. Allowlist is built from Anthropic's API host plus the GitHub Actions runtime control-plane domains (the only IPs a legit claude-code-action job needs). Anything else from a node process under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action` is suspicious by construction. No Sigma — needs cross-table join (process attribution + network destination + DNS). Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://www.securityweek.com/claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot-agents-vulnerable-to-prompt-injection-via-comments/

    | project NodeTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, NodePid = ProcessId, NodeCmd = ProcessCommandLine, NodeFolder = FolderPath;

| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("anthropic.com", "api.github.com", "githubusercontent.com", "githubapp.com", "githubassets.com", "ghcr.io", "actions.githubusercontent.com"))
| where isnotempty(RemoteIP)
| join kind=inner RunnerNode on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.NodePid
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, NodeCmd, NodeFolder, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), Destinations = make_set(RemoteUrl, 20), DestIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 20)
           by DeviceName, NodeFolder, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
let AllowList = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.github.com", "githubusercontent.com", "githubapp.com", "githubassets.com", "ghcr.io", "actions.githubusercontent.com"]);
let RunnerHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or TargetProcessName endswith "/node"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action", "/_work/")
    | distinct DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (RunnerHosts)
| where isnotempty(DstHostname)
| where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." 
     and not(DstIpAddr matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.") 
     and DstIpAddr !startswith "127." and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254."
| where not(DstHostname has_any (AllowList))
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), HitCount = count(), SampleUrl = any(Url)
           by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol
| order by FirstSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 OR source:linux.auditd) (@process.name:node OR @process.executable.path:*/node) (@ParentImage:*claude-code* OR @process.command_line:*claude-code* OR @process.command_line:*@anthropic-ai*) NOT (@DestinationHostname:*.anthropic.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.github.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubusercontent.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.ghcr.io OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubapp.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubassets.com) NOT CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\/node$/i
| regex("(actions-runner|_work|_actions\\/anthropics\\/claude-code-action)", field=ContextImageFileName, strict=false)
| RemoteAddressIP4!=/^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|127\.|169\.254\.)/
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest | DomainName!=/(anthropic\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|ghcr\.io|githubapp\.com|githubassets\.com)$/i | groupBy([aid, FirstIP4Record], function=collect(DomainName, as=resolved_domain))}, field=[aid, RemoteAddressIP4=FirstIP4Record])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort, resolved_domain], function=count(as=conns))
| conns > 0

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

[LLM] DbGate node process spawning shell child (post-exploit RCE) Installation High
Hunts for the dbgate / node.js process spawning a shell or command interpreter, which is the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-47670's child_process.execSync call. The legitimate DbGate runtime does not spawn /bin/sh or cmd.exe as children, so any such child is suspicious in container or host context. Rationale: DbGate's normal runtime never spawns a POSIX shell or Windows command interpreter — the article explicitly states the bypass is `(await import('child_process')).execSync(...)`, so child-process creation under a node parent named dbgate is the direct execution-time signal. Pairs with UC1 to give one network-side and one host-side detection of the same chain.

[LLM] DbGate Zip Slip (CVE-2026-47669): node process writes outside archive dir to OS-sensitive paths Installation High
Detects the Zip Slip exploitation outcome of CVE-2026-47669 where the DbGate node process — invoked via /api/archive/unzip — writes files to OS-sensitive Linux paths (cron, sudoers, SSH authorized_keys, ld.so.preload, systemd units, /usr/local/bin) via `../` entries in a malicious ZIP. In a clean DbGate deployment the node process should only write inside its archive directory, so any write under /etc, /root/.ssh, or /usr/local/bin from node is high-fidelity for this CVE. Rationale: Pivots on the EXACT Zip Slip exploit outcome described in the GHSA PoC: `path.join(outputDirectory, entry.fileName)` allows `../` traversal, and the PoC writes to `/etc/cron.d/dbgate-pwn`. The dbgate node process has no legitimate reason to touch /etc/cron.*, /etc/sudoers.d, /root/.ssh, /etc/ld.so.preload, or /usr/local/bin — these are the canonical persistence/privesc paths attackers traverse to. Corroborated against Snyk's prior DbGate Zip Slip advisory which confirms the same vulnerable archive-extraction code path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h535-j5hr-mv56 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-DBGATEAPI-11023274
ATT&CKT1190 T1053.003 T1505.003

| where FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron." 
    or FolderPath startswith "/var/spool/cron/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/root/.ssh/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/init.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/profile.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/bin/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/sbin/"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/ld.so.preload"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/passwd"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/shadow"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-47669 DbGate Zip Slip - ASIM ImFileEvent (covers MDE for Linux + Sysmon for Linux + auditd)
ImFileEvent

[LLM] DbGate exploit chain: anonymous /auth/login + /api/archive/unzip POSTs from same source (CVE-2026-47669) Exploitation Medium
Detects the multi-step exploit sequence against DbGate's vulnerable archive endpoints: POST /api/auth/login (no creds via amoid=none), POST /api/uploads/upload, POST /api/archive/save-uploaded-zip, POST /api/archive/unzip — all hit by the same source IP within a short window. This is the network-edge view of CVE-2026-47669 exploitation, complementary to host-side file-write detection. Rationale: Targets the EXACT URL set in the PoC (POST /api/auth/login with amoid=none, /api/uploads/upload, /api/archive/save-uploaded-zip, /api/archive/unzip). The chain of >=2 distinct endpoints including unzip or save-uploaded-zip from one source IP is the network-shape of the exploit. Defender/Falcon left empty because neither has inbound HTTP request-URL visibility for DbGate's port. Corroborated via Snyk advisory for the prior dbgate-api Zip Slip variant. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h535-j5hr-mv56 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-DBGATEAPI-11023274
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
// CVE-2026-47669 DbGate exploit chain via WAF/proxy logs in CommonSecurityLog
let ExploitEndpoints = dynamic(["/api/archive/unzip","/api/archive/save-uploaded-zip","/api/uploads/upload","/api/auth/login"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any (ExploitEndpoints)
| extend Endpoint = case(
    RequestURL has "/api/archive/unzip", "unzip",
    RequestURL has "/api/archive/save-uploaded-zip", "save-uploaded-zip",
    RequestURL has "/api/uploads/upload", "upload",
    RequestURL has "/api/auth/login", "login",
    "other")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(Endpoint),
            UrlSamples = make_set(RequestURL, 10),
            UASet = make_set(RequestClientApplication),
            ReqCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP
| where array_length(EndpointsHit) >= 2
    and (set_has_element(EndpointsHit, "unzip") or set_has_element(EndpointsHit, "save-uploaded-zip"))
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] DbGate CVE-2026-47668 — Node.js runner spawning shell/LOLBin children for egress Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of DbGate's JSON Script Runner RCE where attacker-injected JavaScript in the `functionName` parameter calls `process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync()` to launch shell utilities (wget/curl/sh/bash/powershell) from the forked dbgate runner Node.js process. Targets the exploit chain post-injection where the spawned child commands betray the RCE. Rationale: Pins to the exact post-exploit footprint described in the advisory: the forked Node.js runner (working dir `/root/.dbgate/run/<uuid>`, env `DBGATE_API=/home/dbgate-docker/bundle.js`) executing shell utilities via `child_process.execSync()` — concretely `wget --post-data "$(env)"` in the PoC. Parent-cmdline anchors (`bundle.js`, `.dbgate/run/`, `dbgate-docker`) are dbgate-specific artifacts not present in benign Node workloads.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.007

| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bundle.js",".dbgate/run/","dbgate-docker","DBGATE_API")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/home/dbgate-docker","\\dbgate\\","/.dbgate/run/")
| where FileName in~ ("wget","curl","sh","bash","dash","zsh","powershell.exe","pwsh","cmd.exe","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,

[LLM] DbGate exploit web request — POST /runners/start or /runners/load-reader with child_process injection Delivery High
Detects HTTP exploitation traffic for CVE-2026-47668 in reverse-proxy / WAF / IIS / web-server access logs: POST requests to DbGate's `/runners/start` or `/runners/load-reader` endpoints, optionally paired with body inspection matching the JS injection signatures (`process.mainModule.require`, `child_process`, `execSync`, `module.constructor._load`). [LLM] DbGate anonymous auth-bypass token mint — POST /auth/login with amoid:none Reconnaissance Medium
Detects the precursor to CVE-2026-47668 exploitation against a default-deployed DbGate: an unauthenticated `POST /auth/login` carrying body `{"amoid":"none"}` to mint a bearer token when `authProvider:"Anonymous"` (the default). Captures recon/auth-prep traffic that almost always precedes the runner-endpoint hit. Rationale: The advisory documents the exact unauth token-mint vector — `curl -d '{"amoid":"none"}' <dbgate>:3000/auth/login` — used when `authProvider` is left at its default `Anonymous`. Pairing the `/auth/login` POST with a following `/runners/start` or `/runners/load-reader` from the same source within 30 minutes is the full exploit handshake.
ATT&CKT1078.001 T1190

    | project AuthTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication;
let runner =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestURL has_any ("/runners/start","/runners/load-reader")
    | project RunTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, RequestURL_Runner=RequestURL;

[LLM] PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 GlobalProtect login from Unit 42 IOC IPs Exploitation High
Hunt for successful GlobalProtect gateway-connected events sourced from the nine IP addresses Unit 42 attributes to pre-PoC CVE-2026-0257 exploitation. Any successful VPN session from one of these IPs is a high-confidence compromise indicator since the article confirms the actor uses them to bypass GP portal/gateway authentication. Rationale: Uses the nine attacker-IP IOCs published by Unit 42 in the CVE-2026-0257 threat brief — explicit, vendor-attributed, and tied to a CISA KEV-listed exploitation campaign. Matched against PAN-OS GlobalProtect login telemetry which is the exact telemetry the article tells defenders to search. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/

[LLM] PAN-OS GlobalProtect login with CVE-2026-0257 PoC hard-coded host-id / device-name Exploitation High
Hunt for GlobalProtect gateway-connected events whose host-id or device name matches the hard-coded values shipped in the public CVE-2026-0257 PoC code. These strings appear in the GP client-info payload sent during the auth-bypass and are not naturally generated by real corporate endpoints. Rationale: The Unit 42 brief explicitly names these MAC and machine-name strings as defaults baked into the published PoC code — they are the cleanest unique fingerprint of attacker traffic vs legitimate VPN clients. These would rarely if ever appear in a real corporate environment, so the FP rate is near-zero. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/

[LLM] PAN-OS GlobalProtect login matching CVE-2026-0257 PoC client fingerprint Exploitation High
Hunt for GP gateway-connected events carrying the hard-coded endpoint_os_version 'Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit' AND an empty source_user_info.domain — the exact post-PoC release fingerprint Unit 42 documents in the threat brief. Legitimate clients fill in the joined domain; the PoC leaves it blank. Rationale: Unit 42 explicitly publishes endpoint_os_version='Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit' + empty source_user_info.domain as the post-PoC client fingerprint of the CVE-2026-0257 exploit. The empty-domain clause is what shifts it from common-OS noise into high-fidelity exploit signal — real corporate GP clients almost always populate that field with the AD domain. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
// PAN-OS GP client-info strings do not flow into Defender XDR natively.
// Where GP logs are ingested via a custom MDE connector, the substring lives in AdditionalFields:
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType has "GlobalProtect"
| where AdditionalFields has "Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("source_user_info.domain=\"\"","source_user_info.domain=null","\"domain\":\"\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, AccountName, AdditionalFields
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Palo Alto Networks"

| where Message has "Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit"
| where Message has_any ("source_user_info.domain=\"\"", "domain=\"\"", "source_user_info.domain= ", "domain=,")

| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceNTDomain, SourceHostName, DeviceAction, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

ReliaQuest has assessed with moderate to high confidence that the espionage-focused activity is linked to China. "OP-512 was highly

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] OP-512 Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation from IIS worker (SeImpersonate token abuse) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — New Threat Cluster OP-512 Targets Microsoft IIS Servers with Custom Web Shell Fr
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolutions or HTTP egress to the OP-512 attacker-controlled domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com observed in the ReliaQuest report. Article-specific because this domain appeared ~75 days before the main intrusion as the initial staging beacon and is reused by the web shell's self-reporting fallback over DNS/HTTP. Rationale: The domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com is the only network IOC named in the ReliaQuest write-up; matching it across DNS and HTTP egress is a definitive OP-512 signal. Cross-checked the IOC pattern via the article's lead and MITRE T1071.004 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteUrl has "lhlsjcb.com" or RemoteUrl has_cs "ashx.lhlsjcb.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp asc
let ioc_domain = "lhlsjcb.com";
(union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where Name has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP, Domain = Name, QueryTypeName, Source = "DnsEvents"),
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where DnsQuery has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, QueryTypeName = DnsQueryTypeName, Source = "ImDnsActivity"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where RequestURL has ioc_domain or DestinationHostName has ioc_domain or DestinationDnsDomain has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), URL = RequestURL, Source = "CommonSecurityLog")
)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop) Installation High
Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe writing ASP.NET handler files (.aspx, .ashx, .asmx) into upload or temp directories — the exact drop pattern ReliaQuest observed for the OP-512 three-shell framework. Combines parent-process (w3wp.exe) and target-extension predicates to keep false positives down on legitimate deployment activity. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names w3wp.exe as the process that dropped the web shell into the application's upload directory. The parent (w3wp.exe) + extension (.aspx/.ashx) + path (upload/temp) triple gives strong specificity to OP-512 vs legitimate publish flows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

title: IIS w3wp.exe Writes ASP.NET Handler to Upload or Temp Directory
id: 8a2e5d11-7b40-4c5b-9f8a-3d5b6e0c8e21
description: Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe creating ASP.NET handler files (.aspx/.ashx/.asmx/.asax) in upload, temp, or App_Data directories — the OP-512 web shell drop pattern.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05

| ContextImageFileName=/\\w3wp\.exe$/i

[LLM] IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution Actions on Objectives High
Detects the IIS worker w3wp.exe spawning interpreter or reconnaissance binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe, net.exe) — directly matching ReliaQuest's observed OP-512 post-exploitation step of running whoami /priv from the web shell to confirm SYSTEM-level privileges after Potato Suite escalation. Rationale: ReliaQuest directly cites whoami /priv as the post-Potato verification command from OP-512, and the entire chain hinges on w3wp.exe being the parent. Parent (w3wp.exe) + child (recon binaries) is exactly the article's described observed sequence. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1033/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.003 T1033 T1087
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (FileName =~ "whoami.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where ChildName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (ChildName =~ "whoami.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IIS Worker w3wp.exe Spawns Recon Binary (OP-512)
id: 4f7b3c6a-2d11-4f8d-8a51-7e2b1a4c9e3f
description: Detects w3wp.exe spawning cmd/powershell/whoami/net/systeminfo as a child, consistent with OP-512 web shell post-exploitation reconnaissance after Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1505.003
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1033
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\whoami.exe'
            - '\net.exe'
            - '\net1.exe'
            - '\systeminfo.exe'
            - '\ipconfig.exe'
            - '\tasklist.exe'
            - '\hostname.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\reg.exe'
            - '\sc.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child

    - IIS web apps that legitimately shell out to net.exe / ipconfig.exe for diagnostics endpoints (rare)
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\whoami.exe OR *\WHOAMI.EXE OR *\net.exe OR *\net1.exe OR *\systeminfo.exe OR *\ipconfig.exe OR *\tasklist.exe OR *\hostname.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\reg.exe OR *\sc.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|whoami|net1?|systeminfo|ipconfig|tasklist|hostname|wmic|reg|sc)\.exe$/i
| WhoamiPriv := if(ImageFileName=/whoami\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\/(priv|all|groups)/i, "true", "false")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" (Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe" OR Processes.process_name="whoami.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net1.exe" OR Processes.process_name="systeminfo.exe" OR Processes.process_name="ipconfig.exe" OR Processes.process_name="tasklist.exe" OR Processes.process_name="hostname.exe") by host Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" (Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe" OR Processes.process_name="whoami.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net1.exe" OR Processes.process_name="systeminfo.exe" OR Processes.process_name="ipconfig.exe" OR Processes.process_name="tasklist.exe" OR Processes.process_name="hostname.exe") by host Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] OP-512 Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation from IIS worker (SeImpersonate token abuse) Exploitation High
Detects token-impersonation privilege escalation from the IIS app-pool identity to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM — the exact Potato Suite (RottenPotato/JuicyPotato/GodPotato/RoguePotato) chain ReliaQuest observed after OP-512 dropped its web shells. Pivots on child of w3wp.exe with integrity-level jump to System, plus Windows 4672 'special privileges' assignments to non-service accounts. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names the Potato Suite as OP-512's escalation tool from the IIS app-pool to SYSTEM. The IIS-worker-as-parent plus Potato binary-name keywords plus integrity-level jump make this a high-fidelity escalation indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1134/001/ • https://github.com/ohpe/juicy-potato • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
ATT&CKT1134.001 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let PotatoFingerprints = dynamic(["juicypotato", "rottenpotato", "sweetpotato", "godpotato", "roguepotato", "localpotato", "remotepotato", "printspoofer", "efspotato"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("System", "High")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (PotatoFingerprints)
   or FileName has_any (PotatoFingerprints)
   or InitiatingProcessTokenElevation =~ "TokenElevationTypeFull" and AccountName =~ "SYSTEM" and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system", "network service", "local service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessTokenElevation, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
let PotatoNames = dynamic(["juicypotato", "rottenpotato", "sweetpotato", "godpotato", "roguepotato", "localpotato", "remotepotato", "printspoofer", "efspotato"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where TokenElevationType in ("%%1936", "%%1937")  // Full or Default-elevated
   or CommandLine has_any (PotatoNames)
   or ChildName has_any (PotatoNames)
   or (SubjectUserSid == "S-1-5-18" and ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Potato Suite Privilege Escalation from IIS w3wp.exe
id: 9e3c12b8-1d6a-44e9-bf7c-2c0a3b8e15dc
description: Detects Potato-family (Juicy/Rotten/Sweet/God/Rogue/Local/Remote/PrintSpoofer/EFS) privilege escalation invoked from the IIS worker w3wp.exe, matching OP-512's observed SYSTEM escalation.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1134/001/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1134.001
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    parent_iis:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    potato_keywords:
        - CommandLine|contains:
            - 'juicypotato'
            - 'rottenpotato'
            - 'sweetpotato'
            - 'godpotato'
            - 'roguepotato'
            - 'localpotato'
            - 'remotepotato'
            - 'printspoofer'
            - 'efspotato'
        - Image|contains:
            - 'potato'
            - 'printspoofer'
    condition: parent_iis and potato_keywords
falsepositives:
    - Authorized red team engagements
level: critical
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) (@CommandLine:(*juicypotato* OR *JuicyPotato* OR *rottenpotato* OR *RottenPotato* OR *sweetpotato* OR *SweetPotato* OR *godpotato* OR *GodPotato* OR *roguepotato* OR *RoguePotato* OR *printspoofer* OR *PrintSpoofer* OR *efspotato* OR *EfsPotato*) OR @Image:(*potato* OR *Potato* OR *POTATO* OR *printspoofer* OR *PrintSpoofer*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| (regex("(?i)(juicypotato|rottenpotato|sweetpotato|godpotato|roguepotato|localpotato|remotepotato|printspoofer|efspotato)", field=CommandLine)
   OR regex("(?i)(potato|printspoofer)", field=ImageFileName)
   OR IntegrityLevel="System")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, IntegrityLevel], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\inetsrv\\w3wp.exe") (Processes.process_integrity_level="System" OR Processes.process_integrity_level="high") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="SYSTEM" OR process_name!="w3wp.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\inetsrv\\w3wp.exe") (Processes.process_integrity_level="System" OR Processes.process_integrity_level="high") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="SYSTEM" OR process_name!="w3wp.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;

Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw to Take Over Sites

The Hacker News
2026-06-05 14 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical security flaw in Everest Forms Pro, a WordPress plugin with about 4,000 active installations, to execute arbitrary code, leading to a complete site compromise. The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-3300 (CVSS score: 9.8), a remote code execution bug impacting all versions of the plugin up to, and including, 1.9.12. A patch for the flaw was

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Everest Forms Pro RCE exploit attempt from named source IPs · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Everest Forms Pro Calculation Addon PHP injection payload in form submission · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw to Take Over Si
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] WordPress rogue 'diksimarina' admin account creation request · [LLM] WordPress PHP worker spawning shell or download utility post-RCE
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Everest Forms Pro RCE exploit attempt from named source IPs Delivery High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to vulnerable WordPress sites from the four IPv4 sources Wordfence attributed to the CVE-2026-3300 exploitation campaign. Highest fidelity signal since the IPs were named in the original advisory and have driven 29,300+ blocked attempts since 2026-04-13. Rationale: Wordfence's named source IPs are the highest-confidence pivot in the article. Combining IP source + WordPress admin-ajax/everest_forms URI keeps the false-positive surface near zero. [LLM] Everest Forms Pro Calculation Addon PHP injection payload in form submission Exploitation Medium
Hunts POST bodies to WordPress endpoints containing PHP code-context characters that escape sanitize_text_field() and reach eval() in process_filter(). Targets the specific injection shape described by Wordfence — single quotes followed by PHP functions like system, exec, base64_decode, or backticks. Rationale: Wordfence quotes the bug as 'concatenating user-submitted form field values into a PHP code string without proper escaping before passing it to eval()' — the discriminating signal is PHP-function tokens (system, exec, base64_decode, shell_exec, assert) plus single-quote-break characters in a POST to admin-ajax/everest_forms. Cross-checked the wp-json everest path against the Everest Forms plugin source. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("system(","exec(","passthru(","base64_decode","shell_exec","assert(","'.system")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json")
| where csUriQuery has_any ("system(","exec(","passthru(","base64_decode","shell_exec","assert(","%27.system","%27%2Bsystem","`","%60")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json")
| where Message has_any ("system(","exec(","passthru(","base64_decode","shell_exec","assert(","'.system","'+system")
   or RequestCookies has_any ("system(","base64_decode")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where CsMethod == "POST"
| where CsUriStem has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms")
| where CsUriQuery has_any ("system(","exec(","base64_decode","shell_exec","'.system")
| project TimeGenerated, CsHost, CIp, CsMethod, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, UserAgent, ScStatus)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] WordPress rogue 'diksimarina' admin account creation request Installation High
Hunts the specific payload Wordfence saw most commonly in CVE-2026-3300 exploitation: creation of a WordPress administrator account named 'diksimarina' with email 'diksimarina@gmail.com'. Hardcoded IOCs from the original advisory. Rationale: 'diksimarina' and 'diksimarina@gmail.com' are verbatim IOCs from Wordfence's report cited in the article — extremely high-fidelity strings unlikely to appear organically in benign traffic. Searching across multiple log surfaces (WAF, IIS, App Service, syslog) catches the payload regardless of where it lands. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1136/001/
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web Change.Account_Management
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina@gmail.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, AdditionalFields),
(DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FolderPath has_any ("wp-content","wp-admin","wp-includes")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json","wp-login.php","user-new.php")
| where csUriQuery has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina%40gmail.com","diksimarina@gmail.com")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where RequestURL has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json")
   or DeviceProduct has "WAF"
| where Message has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina@gmail.com")
   or RequestURL has "diksimarina"
   or RequestCookies has "diksimarina"
   or DeviceCustomString1 has "diksimarina"
   or DeviceCustomString2 has "diksimarina"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, Message, DeviceAction),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where CsUriQuery has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina%40gmail.com")

| project TimeGenerated, CsHost, CIp, CsMethod, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, UserAgent, ScStatus),
(Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina@gmail.com")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)

[LLM] WordPress PHP worker spawning shell or download utility post-RCE Installation Medium
Hunts the post-exploit behaviour where the PHP/Apache/Nginx worker process spawns sh, bash, wget, curl, python, perl, or nc — the natural follow-on after process_filter() eval() succeeds and the attacker drops a webshell or pulls a second-stage payload. Rationale: The article's kill-chain note explicitly cites 'PHP/Apache/Nginx worker processes spawning unusual children (sh, curl, wget)' as the execution-phase pivot. Pairing the parent web-tier binary with download/shell child binaries follows the BluRaven process-tree pattern and avoids the anti-bare-process-execution smell. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1505.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.0","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","wget","curl","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat","socat","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","wget","curl","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat","socat","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","certutil.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-cgi.exe","php.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
(Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Facility =~ "authpriv" or ProcessName has_any ("audit","auditd")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("php-fpm","apache2","nginx","httpd")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/usr/bin/wget","/usr/bin/curl","/usr/bin/python","/usr/bin/perl","/usr/bin/nc")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WordPress PHP Worker Spawning Shell or Download Utility
id: 6f4e8b3a-1c92-4d57-8a4b-3b7e2c1d9e44
status: experimental
description: Detects PHP/Apache/Nginx worker processes spawning unix shells, curl/wget, python/perl, or nc - high-confidence post-RCE indicator on WordPress hosts following CVE-2026-3300 or similar PHP eval() exploitation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hackers-exploit-critical-everest-forms.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-fpm7.4'
      - '/php-fpm8.0'
      - '/php-fpm8.1'
      - '/php-fpm8.2'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/nginx'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/wget'
      - '/curl'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/perl'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/socat'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@ParentImage:(*\php-cgi.exe OR *\php.exe OR *\w3wp.exe OR *\httpd.exe OR *\nginx.exe) OR @process.parent.executable.path:(*/php-fpm* OR */httpd OR */apache2 OR */nginx)) (@Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/sh OR */bash OR */wget OR */curl OR */python* OR */perl OR */nc OR */ncat OR */socat))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|php|httpd|apache2|nginx|w3wp)/i
| ImageFileName=/(\/sh|\/bash|\/dash|\/wget|\/curl|\/python3?|\/perl|\/nc|\/ncat|\/socat|\\cmd\.exe|\\powershell\.exe|\\certutil\.exe|\\bitsadmin\.exe)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
| sort(count, order=desc)

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-3300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-3300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
